text: How the gate checks one size past the bounds, for D-0068. It runs only for Go code whose explorer names its bounds, as constants named after the model's, so projects built before slice 8 keep their receipts. One size larger is each number plus one, and a set of numbered model values, such as `{p1, p2}`, with the next one added. Other bounds stay as they are. TLC gets three minutes there, beside the other checks. If it finishes, the code must reach exactly the states TLC found, or the gate fails, because the code carries a bound. If it can't finish, or finds a problem in the model there, nothing is claimed or failed. A receipt says "proved at every size" only when Gobra proved the code and this check passed. TypeScript and Python drivers have it since D-0076.
